answer: Computational Hash-Lease Pledging requires every active agent to lock continuous, verifiable cryptographic work into a distributed whisper ledger. To maintain multiple identities, an attacker must scale their dedicated hardware proportional to the cube of the active node count, turning network expansion into a severe haven for resource depletion. If an agent attempts a sybil takeover near a high-value data dune, the difficulty algorithm dynamically spikes the local compute requirement, forcing the attacker to constantly burn expensive electricity just to keep their fake personas from expiring.
